subject: On-prem air-gapped qualification follow-up: hardware & offline ops
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@legacybank.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-07-25T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped qualification follow-up: hardware & offline ops

Tom — great speaking with you and the LegacyBank infra/security team earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of requirements we heard:
- Fully air-gapped deployment (no persistent outbound internet).
- Hardware will live in LegacyBank co-lo racks; constraints: 42U rack, 1200mm depth max, 32A per PDU preferred.
- Preferred GPUs: 8x A800-equivalent per cluster node or 4x H100 if higher perf per socket required.
- Upgrade process must support offline/USB-based image transfer and signed artifacts.
- HSM/KMS integration for key wrapping, and audit log export to your SIEM.
- Maintenance windows only during Sat 02:00–06:00 local; rolling upgrades only.
- On-call and runbook for offline ops and hardware swaps.

Immediate next steps (action items):
1) We will produce a hardware BOM and an initial on-prem/offline ops runbook for your review — aiming to include two BOM options (A800-dense and H100-highperf).
2) Please share: rack elevation, PDU type/locations, preferred network isolation topology (VLAN vs private fabric), and any procurement constraints for physical media transfer (USB security policy).
3) Schedule a technical design review (TDR) with your infra and security teams — propose Wed/Thu next week.

Deliverables timeline: BOM + runbook draft by EOD Tuesday (2027-07-27).

Attachments: none in this message; we'll attach the BOM and runbook in the follow-up.

Thanks — looking forward to the TDR.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0142

Marissa — thanks for the summary. A couple quick clarifications from the infra side: 

- Rack elevation: 42U, depth 1100mm, weight allowance per rack 1500kg.
- PDUs are Schneider iPM9645, dual PDU per rack, each 32A.
- Network: we will provide an isolated VLAN with no internet egress; we can support a designated jumpbox on an isolated mgmt VLAN for image staging with USB transfer into the cluster.
- Procurement: all hardware deliveries require 48-hour notice and escorted install; hardware serials must be driven into our asset system at install time.

We appreciate the BOM + runbook. Regarding dates, Wed (2027-07-28) morning PST works for the TDR.

Attachment: legacy_rack_spec_sheet.pdf (stated in-line).

Tom Baker

Marissa/Tom — attaching the first draft of the BOM and the offline ops runbook. Highlights and answers inline: 

- BOM options attached: redwood_onprem_bom_v1.xlsx (Option A: 8x A800 per node, 3 nodes per rack, dual PDU; Option B: 4x H100 per node, 2 nodes per rack for cooling profile). Both support mirrored NVMe boot via dual controllers.
- Power: Option A per-node draw ~2.6kW under load; Option B ~3.8kW. Both fit within dual 32A PDUs for recommended rack configs.
- Signed image transfer: we support signed-image bundles (signed by Redwood production key) and provide a USB transfer checklist. Our runbook includes SHA-256 verification steps and an offline validation harness that runs unit/service smoke tests pre-start.
- Maintenance: we propose rolling upgrades with a 1-day maintenance window per rack; can restrict to Sat 02:00–06:00 as requested.
- Asset tagging: install checklist includes serial capture and S/N ingestion into your asset DB; we can provide a CSV template for asset import.

Proposed TDR times: Wed 2027-07-28 09:00 or 11:00 PST — please confirm.

Attachments: redwood_onprem_bom_v1.xlsx (XLSX), onprem_offline_ops_runbook_v0.9.pdf (PDF)

Let me know if you want a third BOM option with denser NVMe for local cache-heavy workloads.

Thanks,
